title: Total cost of ownership: licence, integration, operation and the exit

videos.script: Coreto's Platform team runs its own monitoring. Metrics, logs and traces, on machines it looks after itself. A hosted service would do the same job, and its price is on a web page. {{platform}} Put the two prices side by side and running it yourself looks cheaper by a wide margin. That comparison has one line in it. A real one has four. {{lines}} The licence is what the vendor charges. Integration is the work before anything works. Operation is the time people spend keeping it alive, every week. And the exit is what it costs to leave. {{four}} The line that changes the answer is the one nobody invoices. At Coreto, operation is three quarters of what self-hosting costs, and it never appears on a bill. {{hidden}} This lesson builds the four lines in your spreadsheet, three years out. Then it does something most comparisons skip. It prices leaving on the day you sign, while you still have the leverage to make leaving cheap. {{exit}}
